```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(plotly)
cars <- datasets::mtcars
cars$model <- rownames(cars)
cars$cylinders <- factor(cars$cyl, levels = c(4, 6, 8),
                         labels = c("4 cylinders", "6 cylinders", "8 cylinders"))
r <- cor(cars$wt, cars$mpg)
```

## The question

<p class="lead">How does vehicle weight relate to fuel economy?</p>

<div class="metric">32<small>cars in the dataset</small></div>
<div class="metric">1973–74<small>model years</small></div>

Each point on the next slide represents a car. Colour shows cylinder count.

**Navigate:** use the right and left arrow keys, or the slide controls at the bottom. Click outside the chart before using the arrow keys.

<p class="note">Source: R's built-in mtcars dataset, based on 1974 Motor Trend road tests. Historical data, not current vehicle ratings.</p>

## Weight and fuel economy

<p class="note">Hover for a car's details. Drag to zoom. Click a legend label to hide or show a group. Double-click the plot to reset.</p>

```{r interactive-chart}
plot_ly(cars, x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, color = ~cylinders,
        colors = c("#007F73", "#B56500", "#7B4AB5"),
        type = "scatter", mode = "markers", height = 430,
        marker = list(size = 12, opacity = 0.85,
                      line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
        text = ~paste0("<b>", model, "</b><br>",
                       "Weight: ", wt, " thousand lb<br>",
                       "Fuel economy: ", mpg, " MPG (US)<br>",
                       "Gross horsepower: ", hp, "<br>", cylinders),
        hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Weight (thousand lb)", gridcolor = "#e4eaf0"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Miles per US gallon", gridcolor = "#e4eaf0"),
         paper_bgcolor = "#f7fafc", plot_bgcolor = "#f7fafc",
         font = list(family = "Arial", color = "#183244", size = 14),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.12),
         margin = list(l = 75, r = 25, b = 65, t = 50),
         dragmode = "zoom") %>%
  config(displayModeBar = TRUE, displaylogo = FALSE, responsive = TRUE,
         scrollZoom = FALSE)
```

## What the sample shows

<div class="metric">`r sprintf("%.2f", r)`<small>Pearson correlation between weight and MPG</small></div>

Heavier cars generally have lower fuel economy in this sample.

The **`r rownames(cars)[which.max(cars$mpg)]`** has the highest recorded fuel economy at **`r max(cars$mpg)` miles per US gallon**.

Cylinder groups also differ. The chart shows an association, but it cannot isolate the effect of weight from engine design or other factors.

## Explore it yourself

1. Return to the chart using the **left arrow** twice.
2. Click **8 cylinders** in the legend to hide that group.
3. Hover over a light car and a heavy car to compare their MPG and horsepower.
4. Restore the group and drag across a smaller region to zoom in.

<p class="lead">Does the overall pattern remain visible within a cylinder group?</p>
